name: Selegiline
summary: A medicine (an MAO-B inhibitor, sold as Eldepryl and Zelapar) that slows the breakdown of dopamine in the brain. It is used with levodopa in Parkinson's disease, and as a skin patch for depression.
description: Selegiline, sold under brand names including Eldepryl and Zelapar, is a selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) inhibitor. At recommended doses, it slows the breakdown of dopamine in the brain, which boosts dopamine activity. It is used as an add-on to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease to reduce 'wearing-off' symptoms, and as a skin patch to treat major depressive disorder. At higher doses it also blocks MAO-A, which raises the risk of dangerous reactions with tyramine-rich foods.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Selegiline, marketed under brand names including Eldepryl and Zelapar, is a selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) inhibitor. At recommended doses, it reduces dopamine breakdown in the brain, thereby enhancing dopaminergic activity. It is indicated as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease to reduce 'wearing-off' symptoms, and in transdermal form for the treatment of major depressive disorder. At higher doses, it loses selectivity and inhibits MAO-A as well, increasing the risk of dietary tyramine interactions.
